costDetail.src: PA Report 2/2026, section 9 (cost of production ending September FY2026/2027) with item detail from sections 5, 6 and 7
notes: Group totals are the section 9 cost of production figures, printed in whole ringgit: general charges 71 (budget 61), upkeep & cultivation 195 (145), harvesting & collection 91 (90), total ex-estate 357 (296). Per tonne CPO: 367 (317), 1,009 (762), 471 (474), total 1,847 (1,553).

Harvest items are RM/t as printed in section 7 (total RM1,382,342.60 = 79.19/t vs budget to date RM1,763,224.02 = 80.53/t; annual budget RM2,576,529 = 48.36/t). Section 9 prints 91 (budget 90), which does not match section 7.

Upkeep items are the whole-number RM/t printed in the section 6 table (FFB 17,456 t; budget 21,895 t); they match section 9 (195 vs 145). Other (5 items) = census & thinning out, drains, boundaries/survey/fences, supplying, tools: RM26,041 / 17,456.09 t (budget RM48,525 / 21,895 t), calc.

General-charge items are calc: section 5 RM amount x (mature 2,229.74 / total planted 2,299.81 ha) / 17,456.09 t; budget x (2,182 / 2,254 ha) / 21,895 t. This mature-area allocation of cash charges reproduces the printed section 9 figures 71 and 61 (cash charges RM1,282,008 vs RM1,381,215 budget). Depreciation and amortisation (RM1,108,940, budget RM1,129,840) is excluded, as in the section 9 total. Section 5 RM columns are headed 'Actual 5M' but the RM/ha columns 'Actual 4M'; the RM/ha figures (1,040 = 2,390,948 / 2,299.81 ha) are 5-month figures.
Other (25 items) in general charges = the remaining staff, labour overhead, office and premises lines (RM122,818; budget RM182,107).

summary: FY2026/27 to Sep 2026 (5 months): FFB 17,456.09 t vs 21,895 t budget; yield 7.83 t/ha vs 10.03 budget (22% below) and 10.56 in May–Sep 2025 (26% below), blamed on the low-crop first half (PA 2/2026).

Cost RM357/t FFB vs RM296 budget (May–Sep 2026), high because crop fell short: upkeep RM195 vs 145 (manuring material RM92 vs 57, roads RM42 vs 25), general charges RM71 vs 61, harvesting RM91 vs 90 (PA).

Harvesters 119 vs 123 and sprayers 15 vs 20; 11.3 harvesting rounds vs 15 budgeted, 14-day interval, outturn only 59% (harvesters working without muster); sprayers slow (circle 4.3, selective 3.3 ha/man-day): PA wants CDA and mist blowers.
Manuring 79% (3,796.22 of 4,790.79 ha; RP and NK2 late); EFB 123 of 548 ha; circle spraying 58% and selective 95% of budget to Sep 2026; Ganoderma census so far C77 10%, D72 6%, D71 7.4% (PA).
FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026) yield 24.38 t/ha vs 18.81 in FY2024/25 (+30%); May–Jun 2026 3.22 vs 4.11 t/ha (-22%), with 05A and 14D down over 60% (Agro 2-2026).

issues.title: Harvesting cost RM91/t vs RM79.19/t
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 9 prints harvesting & collection RM91/t (budget 90), but the section 7 table gives RM1,382,342.60 / 17,456.09 t = RM79.19/t (budget to date RM1,763,224.02 = RM80.53/t). Section 9 total 357 (296) adds up from its own lines, so the dashboard uses 91; with section 7 harvesting the cost would be lower. General charges 71 (61) and upkeep 195 (145) do reconcile with sections 5 and 6.

issues.title: PA fertiliser programme differs from Agro
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Appendix 2 (FY2026/27) vs Agro 2-2026 Appendix 1: 1999A NK2 2,500 g x3 (PA) vs 2,200 g x3 (Agro); 2003D/E/F/H NK1 2,500 g May and Aug, 1,700 g Dec and Mar vs NK1 2,000 g x3 + 1,500 g Mar; 2002A/B, 2003A/B/C/G NK1 2,000, 2,000, 1,700, 1,700 vs 2,000 x3 + 1,500; 2005A/2006A/2006C Mix A 2,500 Jun, NK1 2,500 Sep, Mix A 2,000 Jan, NK1 2,000 Apr vs Mix A 2,000, NK1 2,000 x2, Mix A 2,000; 2007A/2008A Mix A, BRP 750 g, Mix C, Mix B vs Mix A/NK1; 2013C/2014D/2015B Mix B 2,500 May + BRP 750 Jul + Mix B 2,200 x3 vs Mix B 2,200 x4 + RP 1,500 Jun; 1999C 'Due to Replanting fy27/28' (no programme) vs Agro NK2 2,200 g Nov and Mar (replanting deferred to FY29/30).

issues.title: Harvesting annual budget inconsistent
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 7: harvesting labour budget to date RM1,449,714.02 (5 months) vs annual budget RM1,824,362 (RM34.24/t on 53,279 t), while supervision (RM103,625 of 248,776) and internal transport (RM190,915 of 457,861) are about 42% of annual. Annual total RM2,576,529 = RM48.36/t vs RM80.53/t budget to date.

issues.title: General charges text vs table
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 5.1: upkeep lines/electricity/water 'overspent by 533%' but the table shows RM54,280 vs RM3,540 (+1433%); water/electricity 'overspent by 17%' but the table shows RM336,970 vs RM256,140 (+32%). RM columns headed 'Actual 5M' but RM/ha columns 'Actual 4M' (RM/ha 1,040 = RM2,390,948 / 2,299.81 ha is the 5-month figure); vehicle table also headed 4M for the period ending September.

issues.title: Labour shortage shown as 10, actually 22
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 3: 194 workers vs 216 required, but the +/- total is printed as 10 (sum of harvesters 4, manuring 1, sprayers 5). General workers 15 vs 27 shown as '-' (short 12); van driver and wireman (0 vs 1) and driver utility/store attendant (1 vs 0) also shown as '-'. Text 3.3 says manuring workers adequate at 17 vs 18.

issues.title: Pruning and spraying totals vs text
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 6.6.1 says 2,331 ha of 8,835 ha pruned; the table total is 2,356.4 of 8,835.16 ha (26.67%). 6.3.1 selective budget 2,217.78 ha (1 round) vs the table's one-round area 2,208.79 ha (2,108.22 ha done). Second selective rounds printed as DEC-25 and MAR-25 (should be Dec 2026 / Mar 2027 in FY2026/27); 2000A 'APRL-27'; transferred blocks show '#DIV/0!'. Circle 1,605 ha done matches the table (1,605.42).

issues.title: Palm stands: PA appendices vs Agro
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Appendix 1 (Sep 2026): 289,921 palms, 126 SPH; F55 4,007 palms (79 SPH), F56 4,795 (87), H54 3,646 (74), A63 1,674 (89). Appendix 2 of the same report: F55 6,892 (144), F56 6,891 (144), H54 6,494 (144), 63 670 palms on 5.88 ha. Agro 2-2026 Table 3 (Jun 2026): 303,933 palms, 132 SPH, 03F 132 SPH. Appendix 2 uses older areas (e.g. A01 39.21 ha vs 39.80 in Appendix 1) and prints block 68 stand as 9.31.

issues.title: Manuring appendix rows out of order
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Appendix 2 (pages 70-71): 2003C 36 and 37 and 2002A 24 list Mar 27 first; 2002A 23 starts with an Apr 27 Mix C row (apparently 2008A 64's); 2008A 64 and 65 have no Apr 27 round although 62 and 63 do; 2006D 61 shows only 'Mar 27 NK1 1.70 kg, applied Aug 26' although PA 6.4.4 says sub-surface manuring was done there (Agro: Mix A 8,000 g sub-soil, Jun 2026). Applied months were read top-down.

issues.title: Area statement percentages and planting years
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 2: non-cultivated 219.64 ha shown as 5.93% (it is 8.72% of 2,519.45 ha); streams/drains 8.24 ha and unplantable 62.09 ha shown as 0%; the column totals 97.21%. Appendix 1 lists B82 (Agro: 2023A, mature from FY26/27) under 2024 as mature, and B89 (Agro: P26A-89) under 2024. 12.1 heads PR24 as 54.84 ha; Appendix 1 B85 + B88 = 54.92 ha; CEO table says 49 ha.

issues.title: PA crop table 'last year' columns
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 section 8 'LAST YEAR' has 'Actual same period' 22,413.49 t (2,122.7 ha, 10.56 t/ha) = May–Sep 2025 only, and 'Annual 12 months budget' 45,874.00 t (21.58 t/ha) = FY2025/26 budget, not an actual full year. Neither report prints FY2025/26 full-year tonnage. Same-period hectarage 2,122.7 vs 2,229.74 ha now.

issues.title: Rainfall: PA vs Agro months
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 Appendix 3 vs Agro 2-2026 Table 19 for the same months: May 2026 133 vs 107 mm (8 days both); Jun 2025 189 vs 186 mm; Aug 2025 208 mm/17 days vs 194 mm/16 days; Jan 2026 325 vs 323 mm; Apr 2022 160 mm/11 days vs 188 mm/12 days. PA shows Dec 2017 as 5,667 mm (2017 total 10,338) where Agro has 557 mm.

issues.title: New planting PR26 block naming
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 12.2 'PR26/89B (Ex-Bakau Area) (15 ha)', manuring not due, 10 palms supplied; CEO table item 21 'PR26/69B (ex-Bakau) 16 ha'; PA 1/2026 12.3.2 said PR26/69B (16 ha) was planted April 2026. Agro 2-2026 7.1 (Jun 2026) says P26A-89 (15.15 ha) was still at land preparation, and its Appendix 1(f) gives a programme for 2026A 69(B) on 44.53 ha.

issues.title: Field count and improving fields in Agro yield text
issues.detail: Agro 8.2 and 8.9 refer to 21 fields, but Tables 17 and 18 list 22. Text 8.9 says only four fields improved in May–Jun 2026 (03B, 03C, 03G, 06C); Table 18 also shows 07A up (3.60 to 3.75, +4%).

issues.title: Period 2 labelled June and July
issues.detail: Agro Table 18 is titled 'as of July 2026 (Period 2)' but its column says 'as at June 2026 (Period 2)'; text 8.9 says 'Period 2 (July 2026)'. With the FY starting in May, Period 2 is May–Jun 2026. Agro 5.1.5 says FY26/27 where FY25/26 is meant. Agro Appendix 1(b) column header SEP-25 should be SEP-26; Table 2 labels immature blocks 85/88/89B as 2023A. Agro Table 9 shows 06A April 2026 interval as '13-70' days and 03F Feb 2026 as '16-14' (likely typos).

issues.title: Leaf P values copied from K column
issues.detail: Agro Table 10: P for F55, F56, G42, G43 and H53 is printed as 1.08, 0.99, 1.05, 1.04 and 0.98% — the same as their K values — while text 5.2.3 gives P range 0.160–0.179%.

issues.title: Pruning table errors
issues.detail: Agro Table 11 (FY25/26): 14D actual 183,493 palms vs programme 14,892 (1,232%); without it the actual total would be 433,389, not 616,882 (71%). Table 11 also uses the Dec 2025 palm count 4,964 for 14D (Table 3 shows 4,964 palms for 14D on 71.73 ha at 144 SPH, which is impossible: 4,964 palms, 36.55 ha is sub-block D71 alone in PA 2/2026 Appendix 1; current 14D count 10,343).

issues.title: Palm census: count rose, SPH fell
issues.detail: Agro Table 3: total palms 302,139 (Dec 2025) to 303,933 (Jun 2026), an increase, while text 2.4 reports a 3% reduction in palm stand (it is SPH 135 to 132, on area 2,244.05 to 2,299.78 ha). 03B shown -25% but 159 to 128 SPH is -19.5%; text 2.8 says over 20%.

issues.title: EFB completion 89% vs 91%
issues.detail: Agro 4.3 says 89% of the EFB programme was achieved, but Table 7 shows 21,890.95 of 23,994.61 mt applied (91%) and 24,389.82 mt received (101.6%). Block 49 (698 mt) is listed twice (Aug-25 and Nov-25). Agro shows rates up to 98 mt/ha and block 77 at 435%. Agro 4.5 says an additional 2,160 MT brought the FY25/26 total received to about 26,549 MT, but 2,160 MT is the programme figure in Table 8; Table 8 shows 3,608.17 MT actually received, so the total would be 27,997.99 MT (24,389.82 + 3,608.17).

issues.title: FY26/27 fertiliser programme revised or not
issues.detail: Agro 1.3 says no revision was made to the FY26/27 fertiliser programme; Agro 10.1 and the summary table say it was revised for the changed replanting programme. Contents list Appendix 1 as FY2025/2026 and Appendix 2 as FY2026/2027, but the appendices are FY2026/2027 and FY2027/2028. Table 6 shows the same 49.13 mt applied for both Mix B and NK2.

actions.item: Recruit harvesters (119 vs 123) and sprayers (15 vs 20); 10 workers to be interviewed in Oct 2026
Use CDA for circle spraying (budget next year) and mist blowers for selective spraying (5–6 ha/man-day possible); train spray workers
Monitor herbicide issue and use (glyphosate 1.26 l/ha, Garlon 1.32 l/ha, high); run time-and-motion studies on pumps per man-day
Stop harvesters working without muster attendance (outturn 59%); resolve with the Senior Manager
Raise harvesting rounds (11.3 vs 15 budgeted) and keep intervals under 15 days; review gang allocation in fields over 15 days
End double handling of FFB into bins with the new scissor-lift trailers; consider Super Bull tyred tractors; aim for 3.0 t/man-day
Do not cut unripe bunches; collect oxidised loose fruit (Block 66)
Rat damage census every 3 months after baiting; bait above 10% damage; keep records
Finish the Ganoderma census (C77 10%, D72 6%, D71 7.4% so far); record severity, debole fallen palms; mound blocks above 5%
Re-evaluate sub-surface manuring at P06D/61 (8 bags/man-day, RM27.20/day); consider semi-mechanised application
Catch up delayed FY26/27 manuring (79%, RP and NK2 late) and EFB (123 of 548 ha); compact sub-soil holes in block 61
Spread EFB evenly at 40 mt/ha, not along roadsides; avoid thick piles in young mature (Rhinoceros beetle)
Eradicate woodies, VOPs, Clidemia and Asystasia; standardise herbicide selection
Continue supplying in rehabilitated areas (291 palms to Sep 2026) and rehabilitate the abandoned area at P02/B2
Replace one old water gate this financial year; complete tidal gates and bunds in block 38/39
Monitor high tractor running costs (repairs)
Define general workers' duties to avoid excess overhead (15 vs 27 required)
Extend the contract system to manuring and weeding
Count bunches accurately (unusual bunch-weight jump Sep 2025 to Sep 2026)
Monitor Rhinoceros beetle and treat at threshold; keep Turnera IPM
Keep reclaimed/supply areas as separate sub-blocks for yield records
Block 78 peat: keep water table 50–75 cm; remove necrotic fronds; follow up carbon fertiliser trial
Maintain drainage without over-draining; support recovery in blocks 56, 57, 66
Check soil Ca and acidity; re-test low leaf Ca at next foliar analysis
Stack fronds properly, not in palm circles
Replace abnormal palms, fill vacant points and catch up weeding in immature P24A/P26A
Clear old borate stock
Review the replanting programme
